newsitem.title: FRANCE: French parliament to debate pension funds Thursday.
newsitem.headline: French parliament to debate pension funds Thursday.

text.p: The French parliament will debate a draft law on Thursday introducing pension funds to France, parliamentary papers show.
Government officials were not immediately available for commment on what they expected from the debate, due to run from 1400 GMT to 2030 GMT.

But financial daily L'Agefi said on Monday there was still no agreement on whether the funds could make payouts in a lump sum as well as in annuities, nor over whether pension funds should be obliged to invest a minimum of their assets in shares.
It said government officials had been discussing the pension funds bill with parliamentary deputies over the past week.

The debate is to be based on a draft law drawn up in 1994 by then parliamentary deputies Jacques Barrot, Charles Millon and Jean-Pierre Thomas rather than on proposals drawn up by the finance ministry.
The government however is expected to amend the draft law to bring it nearer to its own proposals.
The finance ministry proposals stipulate that payouts should be in annuities only and fix no minimum for investment in shares or bonds.
The pension funds -- which French officials usually prefer to call retirement savings funds -- will be introduced next year to complement the existing system of universal pensions.
They would be independently managed and probably set up through an agreement between employers and their employees.
Discussion about the introduction of pension funds is being closely watched by financial markets, waiting to see whether it affects the allocation of assets between stocks and bonds.
